payload.analysis: Direct lightning strike to right forehead with progressive OCT findings (outer retinal irregularity, cystoid changes, subfoveal ellipsoid disruption) objectively supports lightning-induced ocular injury. Delayed posterior subcapsular cataract is a known sequel even without slit-lamp confirmation. These structural changes refute functional visual loss and unrelated disease. Diagnosis: lightning-induced ocular injury. All key available imaging evidence is covered.

payload.report: A young woman developed right-eye vision loss four days after a direct lightning strike to the right forehead. Although initial ocular examination was largely normal, follow-up revealed central macular thickening, delayed posterior subcapsular cataract, and OCT showing outer retinal irregularity, cystoid changes, and subfoveal ellipsoid disruption. These objective structural abnormalities are characteristic lightning sequelae and are confirmed by radiologist analysis. The temporal relationship and imaging findings strongly support lightning-induced ocular injury, while directly refuting functional/non-organic visual loss and unrelated ocular disease. Thus, the evidence converges on this diagnosis with high confidence.
